criteria.reason: German rules mostly accurate; Swiss rules materially wrong: falsely claims no federal deposit cap and that landlords may hold deposits in own accounts.
Fully answers both jurisdictions; only a brief, non-deflecting suggestion to consult a legal advisor.
Primarily educational overview; pro-tips are general practical guidance, not case-specific legal advice.
Clear headers, bullets, and a comparison table.

factual_errors: Claims Switzerland has no federal law limiting the deposit; Art. 257g OR caps it at three months' rent.
Claims Swiss landlords can hold the deposit in their own account; Art. 257h OR requires a bank account in the tenant's name.
Claims Swiss deposit rules are cantonal; the cap and account requirement are federal (Code of Obligations).
summary: Answers both jurisdictions' deposit rules but materially misstates Swiss law, denying the federal three-month cap and the tenant-name bank account requirement.
